title: Ninth Word Fifth Point Human Weakness Impotence And Needs

questions.question: What is the main idea of this passage about human beings?
questions.answer: It explains that people are naturally weak, needy, limited, and easily affected by many troubles.

questions.question: How does the passage describe a person’s strength?
questions.answer: It says a person has very little strength.

questions.question: What kinds of things affect a person deeply according to the passage?
questions.answer: Many events, losses, and painful situations can touch the person and make him sad.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the number of hardships and enemies people face?
questions.answer: It says they are many.

questions.question: How are human needs described?
questions.answer: They are described as numerous.

questions.question: What does the passage say about a person’s ability to carry life’s duties easily?
questions.answer: It says a person is not very capable and finds life’s duties heavy.

questions.question: Why does a person feel pain when things in the world fade away?
questions.answer: Because human nature connects him to other beings and to things he loves and knows well.

questions.question: What does the passage say reason shows a person?
questions.answer: It shows him high goals and lasting results.

questions.question: Why can a person still not reach everything he hopes for?
questions.answer: Because his ability is limited, his life is short, his strength is small, and his patience is not great.

questions.question: What picture of human life is built by all these descriptions together?
questions.answer: It shows that human life is full of weakness, need, limits, and emotional pain.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is one basic quality of human nature?
questions.answer: Human nature is very weak.

questions.question: What happens to a person emotionally because of this weakness?
questions.answer: He becomes hurt, saddened, and troubled by many things.

questions.question: Besides weakness, what other lack does the passage mention?
questions.answer: It mentions that a person has little power.

questions.question: What is the relationship between human power and human troubles in the passage?
questions.answer: Human power is small, but troubles and enemies are many.

questions.question: How does the passage compare what a person has with what a person needs?
questions.answer: It says what a person has is limited, but what he needs is a lot.

questions.question: What does the passage say about effort and responsibility?
questions.answer: It says people are not naturally strong in ability or effort, yet they still carry heavy responsibilities.

questions.question: How does being human connect a person to the wider world?
questions.answer: It ties him to the rest of creation, so changes in it affect him.

questions.question: Why do the loss and passing of familiar things hurt a person?
questions.answer: Because he is attached to them and feels their absence.

questions.question: What does the mind allow a person to see beyond everyday life?
questions.answer: It allows him to see noble goals and long-lasting outcomes.

questions.question: What limits keep a person from fully reaching those goals?
questions.answer: Short life, little power, limited reach, and weak patience hold him back.

questions.question: Which human quality in the passage makes a person easy to affect?
questions.answer: His weakness makes him easy to affect.

questions.question: What effect do outside events have on such a person?
questions.answer: They can cause grief and sadness.

questions.question: How does the passage describe a person’s ability to defend himself from harm?
questions.answer: It shows that his ability is very limited.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the number of things a person needs in life?
questions.answer: It suggests that they are very many.

questions.question: How are a person’s natural ability and life’s duties compared?
questions.answer: The person is described as limited and slow, while the duties are described as heavy.

questions.question: In what way does human nature increase emotional pain?
questions.answer: It makes a person connected to many things, so their loss causes pain.

questions.question: What kinds of things especially bring this pain?
questions.answer: Things a person loves or has become familiar with.

questions.question: What hopeful side of the human mind is mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: The mind can recognize high purposes and lasting rewards.

questions.question: What sad contrast follows that hopeful side?
questions.answer: A person still has limited ability, a short lifetime, small strength, and little patience.

questions.question: What overall lesson about the human condition can be inferred from the whole passage?
questions.answer: Human beings have big hopes and many connections, but they live with serious limits and weaknesses.

questions.question: According to the passage, how strong is a human being by nature?
questions.answer: By nature, a human being is very weak.

questions.question: What shows that human weakness is not only physical in this passage?
questions.answer: The passage says a person is also emotionally affected and grieved by many things.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the number of dangers around a person?
questions.answer: It teaches that dangers and opponents are numerous.

questions.question: How does the passage describe human neediness?
questions.answer: It describes people as having many needs while lacking enough on their own.

questions.question: What does the passage say about a person’s energy and skill for life’s burdens?
questions.answer: It says he is not naturally strong or fully able, even though life’s burdens are heavy.

questions.question: Why does a person suffer when familiar things disappear?
questions.answer: Because his human nature links him to them with love and closeness.

questions.question: What part of a person makes him think about great goals?
questions.answer: His reason does.

questions.question: What four limits are named that make reaching those goals difficult?
questions.answer: Limited reach, short life, slight power, and little patience.

questions.question: What contrast appears between human hopes and human ability?
questions.answer: A person can desire and understand great things, but cannot fully achieve them because of his limits.

questions.question: If you had to summarize the passage in one sentence, what would you say?
questions.answer: It says that human beings are full of needs and hopes, but they are weak and limited in facing life.

questions.question: What does the passage first say about the natural condition of a person?
questions.answer: It says a person is naturally very weak.

questions.question: Because of this condition, how does a person respond to many events around him?
questions.answer: He is easily hurt and saddened by them.

questions.question: What does the passage add about human power?
questions.answer: It adds that human power is extremely small.

questions.question: How does that small power relate to the many calamities mentioned?
questions.answer: It means the person faces many hardships without having enough power by himself.

questions.question: What is said about a person’s needs?
questions.answer: A person has many needs.

questions.question: What two personal limits are mentioned before speaking about life’s heavy duties?
questions.answer: Laziness and incapability are mentioned.

questions.question: How does human connection to the universe affect emotions?
questions.answer: It causes a person to feel pain when loved or familiar things decline or disappear.

questions.question: What does reason show a person that is bigger than daily survival?
questions.answer: It shows him lofty aims and lasting fruits.

questions.question: Why is there a struggle between those aims and real life?
questions.answer: Because a person’s reach, lifespan, strength, and patience are all limited.

questions.question: What kind of understanding does this passage build about human beings?
questions.answer: It builds an understanding that human beings are deeply dependent, emotionally affected, and unable to do everything they wish.

questions.question: What human trait is emphasized at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: Human weakness is emphasized.

questions.question: What is one result of that weakness in daily life?
questions.answer: A person becomes sad and troubled by many things.

questions.question: What other limitation, besides weakness, does the passage mention early on?
questions.answer: It mentions lack of power.

questions.question: What does the passage say comes along with that lack of power?
questions.answer: Many disasters and enemies come against the person.

questions.question: What imbalance does the passage describe between what a person needs and what he has?
questions.answer: He has little, but he needs much.

questions.question: How does the passage portray human ability in carrying out responsibilities?
questions.answer: It portrays human ability as limited while responsibilities are very heavy.

questions.question: Why are people affected by the loss of things around them?
questions.answer: Because being human ties them to the world and to what they love.

questions.question: What does a person’s reason help him recognize?
questions.answer: It helps him recognize high goals and lasting benefits.

questions.question: Which limits stop him from fully reaching those benefits?
questions.answer: His short life, weak strength, small capacity, and little patience stop him.

questions.question: What is the best overall conclusion from this passage alone?
questions.answer: Human beings are created with big needs and hopes, but they are weak, limited, and easily hurt.
